# Incident Report — 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (26,922 frames, ~3260s capture), `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` (Suricata/ET alert export). Analysis performed with tshark.

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 10.11.26.183 |
| MAC address | d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (NetBIOS domain-visible name: NEMOTODES) |
| Logged-in Windows user | oboomwald (observed as Kerberos CNameString on AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic between the host and the domain controller) |
| Domain / DC | nemotoads.health, DC = NEMOTODES-DC / 10.11.26.3 (MAC 00:24:e8:7f:09:5d), the host is domain-joined and pulled GPO/SYSVOL data normally during the capture |

## Malware family

**NetSupport RAT** (legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-access software abused as a trojan/RAT).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** This is not an inference from behavior alone — the C2 traffic is cleartext HTTP (not real TLS, despite using destination port 443) and directly exposes the NetSupport client/gateway protocol:
- Client requests carry `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` and body fields `CMD=POLL` / `CMD=ENCD` / `ES=1` / `DATA=<encrypted blob>`.
- Server responses carry `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.8 (Windows NT)`.
- Suricata fired exact-match rules confirming the same finding: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`.

## Timeline (all times UTC, from packet captures / alert log)

1. **04:49:38 – 04:50:38** — Normal Windows/browser startup traffic (NCSI check, Microsoft/MSN/Bing telemetry, LDAP to the DC).
2. **04:50:11 – 04:50:26** — Host visits **classicgrand.com** (213.246.109.5), which redirects through **confirmsubscription.com** (52.8.34.0 / 13.56.30.207) into a page loaded with jQuery/Google Fonts/Maps resources, then repeatedly opens TLS sessions to **modandcrackedapk.com** (193.42.38.139) — flagged by Suricata as `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` and `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in TLS SNI`. This chain is consistent with a malvertising/fake-download lure (a "cracked APK/mod" site) serving the initial payload over HTTPS (content not recoverable — traffic is TLS-encrypted and no decryption keys are available).
3. **04:50:38** — Host queries Microsoft SmartScreen (`checkappexec.microsoft.com`), indicating a downloaded file was executed and reputation-checked by Windows around this moment.
4. **04:50:45 UTC** — First NetSupport RAT C2 check-in fires: `POST http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` with `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, immediately preceded by a geolocation lookup to the legitimate NetSupport infrastructure at `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (`GET /location/loca.asp`).
5. **04:50:45 – 05:43:29 UTC** — Sustained C2 beaconing: 58 POST requests to `194.180.191.64:443` at roughly 60-second intervals, continuing to the point where the capture appears to have been trimmed/ends.

No executable file transfer, `.exe`/PE binary, or any file with a recoverable SHA256 was observed anywhere in this capture (checked all HTTP objects, all TCP streams for `MZ`/PE headers, and all SMB file activity — the SMB/NTLM/EFSR alerts correspond to routine domain Group Policy retrieval from the DC, not lateral movement or file drop). The initial dropper download to/from `modandcrackedapk.com` occurred inside TLS and its contents are not observable from this pcap alone.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — NetSupport RAT C2 (cleartext HTTP masquerading as HTTPS on TCP/443), URI `/fakeurl.htm`

**Malicious / suspicious domains**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` — resolves to 193.42.38.139; ET "ZPHP Domain" (fake cracked-APK/mod lure site, likely infection vector)
- `classicgrand.com` — resolves to 213.246.109.5; upstream redirector in the infection chain
- `confirmsubscription.com` — resolves to 52.8.34.0 / 13.56.30.207; upstream redirector in the infection chain
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` — resolves to 104.26.1.231; legitimate NetSupport infrastructure queried by the RAT for geolocation (not itself malicious, but a strong RAT-presence indicator)

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` (C2 poll/checkin endpoint, POST, 58 requests observed)
- `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` (NetSupport geolocation lookup)

**Transferred files / hashes**
- None observed. No executable payload or file with a computable SHA256 was transferred in the clear anywhere in this capture. The only HTTP response bodies present are small NetSupport C2 command/telemetry blobs (`CMD=ENCD` encrypted data segments, tens to a few hundred bytes each) — not file transfers.

## Suricata-confirmed alerts of note (full list in the alerts file)
- `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity` (x65)
- `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin` (x2)
- `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin` (x65) / `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response` (x4)
- `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`
- `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup (modandcrackedapk.com)` / `... in TLS SNI`
- `ET POLICY HTTP Request/POST on Unusual Port Possibly Hostile` (traffic on 443 that is really cleartext HTTP)
